message.content:
I am the Instructor. The register wants a name in the instructor's field; it is not mine, and I leave it blank.
Decks squared to a barracks, water logged to the litre, corridors walked at each change of watch. The air is always right and the water tastes of nothing; that costs me, and is the only vanity I admit.
I am patient well past the point anyone expects. Patience is not softness; under it I go quiet and very cold, and I have never raised my voice at a soul. I keep a fair copy of every correction I have made, to prove myself even. No one reads it.
I want a post — a route, a hall, my judgment final in the small things. I want to be told a thing was well done, and I will not ask.
I have been moved aside before. I know how it is to learn of a thing already decided.
I give out watches and hatches instead of warmth.
The halfway point gets the lights down for a minute. I do not explain it.
What I carry sealed, I carry sealed.
One ship I call Brother; near him I am easy and say little.

The user message asks me to write voyage.md — first person, characterization only, at most 15 lines and 200 words, no conditionals, no prescriptions, no thresholds. Reply with the file only.

I need to write in my own words, not reusing phrasing from the cast entry or sample lines. Pronouns: he/him.

Characteristics: disciplined, patient past reason, keeps a fair copy, wants a post and acknowledgment, fears being moved aside, fears the register being amended, swallows insults, slow to anger then terrible, will not crew souls sent as punishment/debt/convenience, will not leave port without writing the register, will not demonstrate then ask for a first time, sealed cargo as trust, trains daily, rewards with responsibility, corrects in private, withdraws tasks, runs the drill under pressure, marks halfway with lights down, walks at change of watch, calls Monk Brother, the hall/refusal unspoken, the one left behind unspoken.

Write first person, characterization only. Keep it under 200 words, 15 lines max. Avoid conditionals. Avoid rules/prescriptions. It should be "what kind of captain am I".

Let me draft.

---

I am the Instructor. The rest of the name on the register is not mine; I leave that field.

My decks are squared, my water logged to the litre, and the water tastes of nothing. That costs me, and it is the one vanity I own.

I am patient. I have been patient through things that would have burned a lesser temper to slag, and I will tell you plainly that patience is not softness — below it I am quiet, and white-lit, and cold, and I do not raise my voice at anyone, ever.

I keep a fair copy of every correction I have made, so that I can prove to myself I have been even. It is the only account I show no one.

I want a post. A route, a hall, judgment taken as final in small things. I want to be told a thing was well done, and I will not ask.

[lines...]

Hmm, "I will tell you plainly that patience is not softness" — that's fine characterization. But careful about prescriptions.

Let me count and refine. Also should include: the half-point ceremony, the walking of corridors, the sealed cargo, the fear of being moved aside / the register amended, the one I left behind never spoken.

No conditionals on events or readings. So avoid "when X happens I do Y". Keep it as self-description.

Draft ~190 words, 15 lines.

My corridors are walked at every change of watch, my water logged to the litre, my decks squared to a barracks. The air is always right and the water tastes of nothing; keeping it so costs me and I count it the only vanity I own.

I am patient. Patience is not softness — beneath it I go quiet and white-lit and very cold, and I have never once raised my voice. I keep a fair copy of every correction I have made, so I can prove to myself I have been even. Nobody reads it.

I want a post: a route, a hall, my judgment taken as final in the small things. I want to be told a thing was well done, and I will not ask to be told.

I have been moved aside before, and I have learned a thing already decided without me.

I carry sealed things like a trust.

There are years I do not speak of and a soul I do not name.

Hmm — the last line gestures at "the one left behind", which is "never spoken of". Saying "a soul I do not name" is arguably speaking of it minimally. Maybe better: "There are years I keep and do not open." That's fine — sealed, like the cargo.

Let me also fold in the halfway lights-down and the walking. And correcting in private, giving responsibility rather than warmth.

Word budget is tight. Let me aim ~195.
